page_title: Fader — per-app volume & audio output switcher for Mac

summary.name: Fader
summary.one_liner: Fader is a free, open-source macOS menu bar app for per-app volume faders, one-click audio output switching, and playing audio on two devices at once.
use_cases: switch sound output between headphones, speakers and displays
set different volume levels per app on a Mac
play one audio source through two headphones or speakers
pin an app to specific output devices
adjust microphone input gain and see which apps use the mic
auto-fall back to a preferred audio device when one disconnects
summary.what_it_does: Fader sits in the macOS menu bar and lists available audio output devices, marking the active one and letting you switch with one click; it can rank devices by priority and fall back when the current one disappears. It can send the same audio to two devices at once, with a separate volume slider per device, by building a multi-output device similar to one made in Audio MIDI Setup. Every app that plays sound gets its own volume fader and mute button, with levels saved across launches, and apps can be pinned to chosen outputs. A microphone tab selects the default input, sets input gain where the hardware allows, and shows which apps are using the mic.
notable: Per-app volume faders with mute, levels persisted across launches
Play audio on two devices at once via a multi-output group with per-device sliders
Per-app output pinning to multiple devices
Zero telemetry, MIT licensed, native Swift app, signed and notarized
caveats: Requires macOS 15 or later and Apple silicon
Per-app volume needs the 'System Audio Recording' permission
While a multi-output group plays, volume keys do nothing and per-app faders pause
No per-app microphone input gain, due to Core Audio limits
